text:
Maya Patel: Quick Q — seeing a spike of 429s from hosted during streaming tests. We're using the JS SDK with chunked responses and Swift mobile client with long-poll fallback. Any recommended retry rules? Specifically: how to treat 429 vs 5xx for streams, and idempotency keys for resumable streams?

Jay Huang: Do you have the request pattern? are these short bursts or sustained? @Maya Patel

Maya Patel: Mostly short bursts after sending ~4 concurrent streams from load test. 429s come back with Retry-After in seconds sometimes, sometimes not. logs: 429 x3 then 5xx.

Tom O'Leary: For non-streaming, we treat 429 as retriable with expo backoff + respect Retry-After. For streaming it's trickier — can't just re-POST without idempotency key or resume token.

Priya Shah: Quick checklist:
- Use idempotency-key on initial create if your API supports it
- For streaming resume prefer server-issued resume_token in stream frames
- If you get 429 before any user-visible tokens, retry with backoff

sdk-bot: Recommended client behavior:
```
if (status == 429) {
  if (hasRetryAfter) wait(retryAfterSeconds)
  else backoff = jitteredExponential(base=200ms, cap=10s)
  retry(count < 5)
}
if (5xx) retry with expo backoff but cap retries lower (3)
if (non-idempotent && no idempotency-key) do not retry POST
```

Maya Patel: For Swift specifically, any tips for streaming reconnect? we can stash partial response but don't want duplication.

Jay Huang: If server provides resume_token include it in reconnect payload to continue. If not, treat as a full restart but require idempotency-key so server can dedupe.

Priya Shah: Also monitor token-level cost — repeated restarts cost tokens. Add a circuit-breaker window: if >X errors in Y seconds, fail fast and surface to app.

Tom O'Leary: Edge cases: 429 bursts from auth refreshes — client should coordinate single refresh and queue other requests. Also respect "Retry-After" even if tiny.

Maya Patel: Thanks. I'll send a small PR to the JS SDK to clarify: 1) always honor Retry-After, 2) use jittered expo, 3) do not auto-retry non-idempotent POSTs without idempotency-key. Ping @Jay to review.

Jay Huang: SGTM, quick code nudge: use decorrelated jitter (see link) https://www.awsarchitectureblog.com/2015/03/backoff.html :thumbsup: 

Maya Patel: PR posted: https://git.redwood.dev/r/1234 — tests included. Will file follow-up for Swift pattern.

sdk-bot: If anyone wants, I can add a small doc snippet to devex on recommended patterns.

Priya Shah: Please do. Also let's add a note in the mobile cookbook about resume tokens vs idempotency keys.

Maya Patel: Thanks all :pray:
